title: Monomial classification of homogeneous additive polynomials
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $n\ge0$, and let $P=k[Z_1,\ldots,Z_n]$ be the polynomial ring [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring] with the grading by total degree [def-pc-standard-graded-algebra]. Let $d>0$ and let $0\ne f\in P_d$. Say that $f$ is additive if the identity $f(Z+W)=f(Z)+f(W)$ holds in the polynomial ring over $k$ on the two disjoint tuples $Z,W$. Write $\operatorname{char}k$ for the characteristic of $k$ [def-pc-field-characteristic]. If $\operatorname{char}k=0$, then $f$ is additive if and only if $d=1$ and $f=\sum_{j=1}^n a_jZ_j$ for coefficients $a_j\in k$. If $\operatorname{char}k=p>0$, then $f$ is additive if and only if $d=p^a$ for some integer $a\ge0$ and $f=\sum_{j=1}^n a_jZ_j^{p^a}$ for coefficients $a_j\in k$.

source.place: Supporting external source read online: Dietel, A refinement of Hironaka’s additive group schemes for an extended invariant (2014), Proposition 3.3.5, printed pp.40–41, https://d-nb.info/1068056037/34; positive-characteristic notation in Definition 1.4.1, p.17. Archival copy WANTED. ILO VIII 2.3.13 is the ancestor motivation only; no Stacks tag states this polynomial classification.

proof.text:
Assume additivity. By the polynomial-ring definition, substitution into the identity is an algebra homomorphism. Put $V_j=(0,\ldots,0,Z_j,0,\ldots,0)$. Starting from $f(0)=0$ (substitute $Z=W=0$), apply the identity successively to $V_1+\cdots+V_{j-1}$ and $V_j$; induction on $j$ gives $f(Z)=\sum_j f(V_j)$. Homogeneity in total degree means that each surviving monomial in $f(V_j)$ is $Z_j^d$, so $f=\sum_j a_jZ_j^d$. Since $f
e0$, some $a_j
e0$. If $n=0$, the sum is empty and contradicts $f
e0$, disposing of that case.

proof.text: Fix $j$ with $a_j\ne0$, and substitute $Z=Xe_j$, $W=Ye_j$ into additivity. The result is $a_j((X+Y)^d-X^d-Y^d)=0$ in $k[X,Y]$. Apply [lem-pur-commutative-ring-binomial-expansion] and compare the coefficient of $X^rY^{d-r}$, for $0<r<d$. By the unique monomial coefficients in the polynomial-ring definition it is $a_j\binom dr=0$. Multiplication by $a_j^{-1}$ in the field gives $\binom dr\cdot1_k=0$.

source.place: Agent coefficient proof supporting Dietel (2014), Proposition 3.3.5, printed pp.40–41, read online at https://d-nb.info/1068056037/34; archival copy WANTED. ILO VIII 2.3.13 is ancestor motivation only.

proof.text: If $\operatorname{char}k=0$ and $d>1$, take $r=1$ in the preceding coefficient equation to get $d\cdot1_k=0$, contradicting characteristic zero; thus $d=1$. If $\operatorname{char}k=p>0$, then $p$ is prime: a nontrivial factorization of the least positive integer killing $1_k$ would give two nonzero elements of a field whose product is zero. For an integer $N\ge0$, $N\cdot1_k=0$ is equivalent to $p\mid N$ by [def-pc-field-characteristic]. Hence $p\mid\binom dr$ for all $0<r<d$. Apply [lem-trf-binomial-vanishing-prime-power] to obtain $d=p^a$ with $a\ge0$; together with step 1 this proves necessity in both characteristics.

proof.text: Conversely, linear forms satisfy the identity by distributivity. In characteristic $p>0$, apply [def-weil-ring-frobenius] to the commutative ring $k[Z_1,\ldots,Z_n,W_1,\ldots,W_n]$, in which $p\cdot1=0$. Its $a$-fold Frobenius iterate is the ring homomorphism $b\mapsto b^{p^a}$, so $(Z_j+W_j)^{p^a}=Z_j^{p^a}+W_j^{p^a}$. Multiply each equality by $a_j$ and sum over $j$ to obtain $f(Z+W)=f(Z)+f(W)$. The iterate for $a=0$ is the identity, including degree one.
